title: I-Team: License Plate Covers Still for Sale at Big-Name Stores, Despite NYC Ban
summary: Despite a New York City law passed last spring banning the sale of items that obscure license plates, the I-Team found major auto parts retailers like AutoZone, Advance Auto Parts, and AutoPlus still selling plastic plate covers. Council Member Robert Holden, who authored the law, highlighted that these covers are used by drivers to evade tolls and red-light cameras, costing the MTA millions annually. While Advance Auto Parts pledged to remove them, other companies have not yet responded to inquiries, and Holden plans to push for increased penalties and more enforcement.

title: AerCap celebrates the delivery of its 50th 737-800 Boeing Converted Freighter
summary: AerCap Holdings N.V. has reached a significant milestone by delivering its 50th 737-800 Boeing Converted Freighter (BCF). This converted aircraft was redelivered to GOL Linhas Aéreas to support a Latin-American e-commerce company's logistics, highlighting the growing demand for express air cargo. AerCap Cargo, a launch customer for the 737-800BCF program, emphasized the aircraft's versatility and reliability in meeting e-commerce logistics needs.

title: 2 Seattle CEOs rank among the nation's 3 best paid
summary: In 2021, two Seattle-based CEOs, Peter Kern of Expedia Group and Andy Jassy of Amazon, were among the nation's three highest-paid CEOs in the S&P 500. Kern topped the list with $296.2 million in total compensation, while Jassy was third with $212.7 million. These figures include cash, stocks, and stock options, and further compensation data for 2022 is anticipated later this year.

title: We Finally Know Where 'Westworld' Will be Available to Stream
summary: Warner Bros. Discovery has announced that several of its series, including "Westworld," will be available on Free, Ad-Based Television (FAST) streamers Tubi and Roku. This move comes after the company's merger led to cancellations and removals from HBO Max. While ads may be present, this offers a free alternative for viewers and could benefit FAST streamers by adding high-profile content to their libraries.

title: 10 Companies Who Inspire Creative Team Collaboration
summary: This article highlights ten companies that excel at fostering creative team collaboration. It explains how these businesses, ranging from tech giants like Google and Amazon to entertainment powerhouses like Disney and Blizzard Entertainment, prioritize open communication, diverse perspectives, and inclusive environments to drive innovation and achieve shared goals. The article emphasizes that creative collaboration is crucial for developing new ideas and products, leading to a sense of shared ownership and motivation among team members.

title: Rivian to lay off 6% of its workforce as EV price war concerns grow
summary: Rivian announced it will lay off 6% of its workforce to conserve cash amidst growing concerns of an EV price war, following price cuts by competitors like Tesla and Ford. CEO RJ Scaringe stated that these cuts would not affect manufacturing jobs at the company's Illinois factory. Despite a successful IPO, Rivian's shares have significantly dropped, prompting a focus on operational efficiency and profitability while ramping up production of its vehicles.

title: Your Guide to the Blink EV Charging Network
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to the Blink EV charging network, detailing its operations, number of stations in the U.S., how to find and use stations, charging speeds, and cost. It explains that Blink is involved in the design, manufacturing, ownership, and operation of its charging stations and offers both Level Two and DC Fast Charging options. The guide also covers payment methods and helps users determine when a Blink station might be the most suitable option for their EV charging needs.

title: AMZN Earnings: All you need to know about Amazon’s Q4 2022 earnings results
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) reported its Q4 2022 earnings, with net sales increasing 9% year-over-year to $149.2 billion, beating expectations. However, net income significantly dropped to $0.3 billion, or $0.03 per share, from $14.3 billion in the prior year, causing the stock to fall 5% in after-market hours. For Q1 2023, Amazon projects net sales between $121-126 billion.

title: Checkout.com expands into US, picks CFO from within
summary: Checkout.com, a global payments solution provider, has appointed Nirupam Sinha as its new CFO as part of its strategy to expand into the US market. Céline Dufétel, the former CFO, will transition to president and COO, overseeing operational and go-to-market teams. The company aims to challenge fintech giant Stripe in the US, emphasizing its similar services and a recent partnership with GE Healthcare.

title: What Was Paul Allen's Net Worth?
summary: This article details Paul Allen's net worth, his journey to becoming a billionaire, and his diverse investment portfolio beyond co-founding Microsoft. It highlights his significant contributions to real estate, art collection, sports team ownership, and various philanthropic endeavors, emphasizing his lasting legacy as a visionary entrepreneur and generous benefactor.

title: Samsung’s next frontier: XR in partnership with Qualcomm, Google
summary: Samsung Electronics is partnering with Qualcomm Technologies and Google LLC to enter the extended reality (XR) device market, which is projected to reach $1.39 trillion by 2030. This collaboration aims to challenge other Big Tech firms like Meta and Apple in the rapidly growing XR space. Although specific product details were not revealed, industry watchers expect Samsung to develop XR headsets utilizing Qualcomm's chipsets and Google's Android operating system, leveraging their existing smartphone collaboration.

title: HubSpot, Pinterest Add to Tech Layoff Chaos
summary: HubSpot and Pinterest have joined other major tech companies in announcing layoffs, with Pinterest cutting 150 employees (less than 5% of its workforce) and HubSpot letting go of around 500 staff (7% of its total workforce). These cuts reflect a continuing trend of mass layoffs in the tech sector due to a tumultuous 2022 and an uncertain economic climate, with over 82,000 tech workers laid off since the beginning of the year. Companies are implementing various cost-cutting measures, but the stream of layoffs is expected to continue for some time.

title: Dollar General Corp. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: Dollar General Corp. (DG) stock fell 1.83% on Thursday, closing at $231.31, despite a mixed trading session with the S&P 500 rising. The stock underperformed several competitors, including Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) which rose, and Walmart Inc. (WMT) and Costco Wholesale Corp. (COST) which had varied performances. This decline ended a two-day winning streak for Dollar General, leaving it $30.90 below its 52-week high.

title: Tom Kingsbury’s Challenge as New CEO of Kohl’s
summary: Tom Kingsbury has been appointed the new CEO of Kohl’s, facing the significant challenge of turning around the $19 billion company amid declining market share and a softening retail climate. He is expected to continue the strategies of his predecessor, Michelle Gass, focusing on active and casual assortments, Sephora partnerships, and smaller store formats, while also potentially bolstering private labels and refreshing stores. Kingsbury, a retail veteran instrumental in Burlington's success, has the support of activist shareholder Macellum Advisors, who pushed for his appointment and have now entered a cooperation agreement.

title: Gap Inc. Wants to Outsource Warehousing for SMBs
summary: Gap Inc., through its GPS Platform Services, is partnering with UPS-owned Ware2Go to provide outsourced warehousing and fulfillment solutions for small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). This collaboration aims to offer SMBs access to enterprise-level supply chain capabilities, including advanced technology, automation, and a network of over 35 warehouses, enabling fast fulfillment and allowing businesses to focus on marketing and product development. The initiative builds on a growing trend of co-warehousing, where SMBs share resources to achieve cost savings, operational efficiency, and better technology access, following similar models adopted by companies like Amazon and American Eagle Outfitters.

title: Netflix deletes new rules on account sharing after public outrage, says US customers yet to be affected
summary: Netflix deleted new rules regarding account sharing from its website after facing significant public backlash. The company clarified that the detailed rules, which sparked outrage, were mistakenly updated for countries outside of Chile, Costa Rica, and Peru, where they are already in place. Although the company still plans to introduce account sharing restrictions for U.S. customers by March 2023, the exact nature of these rules remains unclear following the controversy.

title: Sysco Corp. stock falls Friday, still outperforms market
summary: Sysco Corp. (SYY) stock fell 0.53% to $76.72 on Friday, February 3, 2023, while still outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also decline. Despite its losses, Sysco's stock performed better than competitors like Amazon.com Inc., Walmart Inc., and Costco Wholesale Corp. Trading volume for Sysco was 3.3 million, exceeding its 50-day average.

title: State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY), including its stock price, key statistics, top holdings, and dividend information. It highlights XLY's portfolio value, turnover rate, and its largest positions in companies like Amazon, Tesla, and Home Depot, based on its latest N-PORT filing. The report also includes historical performance data, fundamental charts, and recent trading actions within the ETF's portfolio.

title: What ‘Digital First’ Means for Church & Dwight
summary: Church & Dwight's "digital-first" strategy, highlighted by the successful acquisition of the Hero brand and a significant increase in e-commerce sales, is driving its growth. The company is investing heavily in digital marketing (70% of its spend) and comprehensive employee training to elevate its "digital IQ" across all departments. This approach aims to make digital a business builder rather than just a capability, leveraging sustained post-pandemic consumer behavior towards online shopping.

title: News | Amazon’s HQ2 Set To Open This Year in Northern Virginia Even As Tech Giants Scale Back
summary: Amazon's HQ2 in Northern Virginia is on track to open its initial phase this year, despite other tech giants scaling back operations and laying off employees. The first phase of the megadevelopment is scheduled to debut in summer 2023, with Amazon already having hired over 5,000 employees for the location. This progress contrasts with other tech companies like Google and Microsoft, which are reducing their office footprints.

title: The 7 most in-demand tech skills for freelancers—many pay more than $125 an hour
summary: Despite recent tech layoffs, the demand for tech skills remains high, creating significant opportunities for freelancers. Career experts and platforms like Upwork highlight a "skills gap" where employers struggle to find talent. This article identifies seven in-demand tech skills for freelancers, including full stack development, mobile app development, web design, UX/UI design, CMS development, manual testing, and scripting/automation, with many commanding hourly rates exceeding $125.

title: NLRB: Apple illegally interfered with employees’ protected activity
summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) has found merit in five charges against Apple, alleging the company violated the National Labor Relations Act by interfering with employees' protected activities. The charges include violations related to work rules, handbook rules, confidentiality policies, and specific statements and conduct by high-level executives that "reasonably tend to interfere with, restrain, or coerce employees in the exercise of their right to protected concerted activity." If Apple and the charging parties do not settle, the NLRB's regional director will issue a complaint and pursue the charges before an administrative law judge.

title: CEBA: Energy Customers Announce Record-High of Nearly 17 GW of Clean Energy in 2022, Despite Policy and Market Challenges
summary: In 2022, commercial and industrial energy customers procured a record-breaking 16.9 gigawatts of new clean energy deals, as announced by CEBA. Amazon led the list for the third consecutive year, with General Motors achieving its second-highest annual deal volume. The report highlights a significant commitment to decarbonization, with 54% of participating customers being new to the market, and CEBA's community having catalyzed 64.5 gigawatts of clean energy since 2014, surpassing their 2025 goal.

title: Oracle Named a Leader in Two Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ Reports: iPaaS and Data Integration
summary: Oracle has been recognized as a Leader in both the 2023 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS) and the 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools. This marks Oracle's sixth consecutive leadership position in iPaaS and fourteenth in data integration. The article highlights Oracle's comprehensive integration capabilities, cost-effectiveness, and ability to address diverse customer needs across various environments.

title: Oracle to invest $1.5 bn in Saudi Arabia, open data centre in Riyadh
summary: Oracle Corp plans to invest $1.5 billion in Saudi Arabia to expand its cloud footprint, including opening a third public cloud region in Riyadh and expanding its existing Jeddah facility. This investment aligns with Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 to diversify its economy and attract foreign direct investment, with Oracle also securing contracts for the NEOM project. Saudi officials are pressuring international companies to establish regional headquarters in the kingdom to secure government contracts.

title: Sonos Is Having a Secret Sale Ahead of President's Day
summary: Sonos is holding a "secret sale" on its popular speakers and soundbars ahead of President's Day and the Super Bowl, offering significant discounts. Highlighting the rarity of Sonos sales and their premium status, the article details deals on products like the Sonos Arc and Sonos Beam Gen 2, recommending them for home theater upgrades. The sale includes individual speakers and immersive sets, but the duration and inventory are limited.

title: Software company Autodesk lays off 250 employees
summary: Autodesk, a software company, has laid off 250 employees, which is less than 2% of its global workforce. This decision is part of its fiscal year 2024 plans to align resources with key priorities and comes amidst a global economic downturn affecting many tech companies. The affected roles include digital marketing, technical marketing, and web optimization, though the company continues to hire for other key positions.

title: NetApp adds storage buying options, arrays
summary: NetApp is expanding its storage offerings with new buying options, hybrid cloud capabilities for VMware workloads on Google Cloud, and upcoming QLC all-flash arrays. The NetApp Advance portfolio introduces programs like the Storage Lifecycle Program and Cloud Advantage Program to provide flexibility for on-premises hardware refreshes and cloud storage migrations, positioning NetApp in closer competition with Pure Storage. A new line of all-flash QLC-based arrays, the AFF C-Series, and an AFF A-Series model for remote offices are set to debut in March.

title: NFL extends Zebra next gen data partnership until 2025
summary: The NFL has extended its data partnership with Zebra Technologies until the end of the 2025 season. Zebra will continue to supply live insights from on-field tracking devices which feed into the NFL's Next Gen Stats, enhancing broadcasts and digital experiences for fans. This partnership, ongoing since 2015, also provides valuable data for coaches and league rule evaluations.

title: 4.9 Million Fabuloso Bottles Recalled for Bacteria Risk (Published 2023)
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled approximately 4.9 million bottles of Fabuloso cleaning products due to a bacteria risk. The recall affects products sold between December and January, as an inadequate amount of preservative during manufacturing may have allowed bacteria like Pseudomonas aeruginosa to grow. While generally not harmful to healthy individuals, this bacteria can cause serious infections in those with weakened immune systems or underlying health conditions.

title: CVS Reaches $10.6 Billion Deal to Buy Clinic Owner Oak Street Health - WSJ
summary: CVS Health Corp. has agreed to acquire Oak Street Health Inc. for approximately $10.6 billion, including debt, in an all-cash deal for $39 a share. This acquisition is part of a broader trend of health insurers integrating with primary care providers and will expand CVS's healthcare offerings by adding Oak Street Health's network of 169 senior-focused clinics and 600 healthcare professionals. The deal is expected to close in 2023 and follows CVS's previous acquisition of Signify Health Inc.

title: Mobile App Development market, it is estimated to increase at the rate of more than 23.80% from 2020 to the end of the year 2030
summary: The global mobile app development market is projected to reach approximately USD 366.93 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 23.80% from 2022 to 2030. This growth is driven by the increasing use of smartphones and other gadgets, the leveraging of mobile applications by e-commerce and social media platforms, and the declining cost of data services coupled with rising internet penetration. North America is expected to generate the highest revenues, while the Asia Pacific region is anticipated to show the highest CAGR.

title: Cure imaging storage challenges in the medical cloud
summary: This article discusses the challenges healthcare organizations face with storing and managing vast amounts of medical imaging data, which constitutes 90% of all medical data worldwide. It proposes a solution using NetApp ONTAP and Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP to move medical imaging data to the cloud, offering benefits like cost-effectiveness, enhanced data protection, and improved accessibility for AI/ML analytics and research. The solution also aids in sustainability efforts and ensures compliance, enabling a seamless transition from on-premises storage to the cloud.

title: Don’t use these cleaners: Millions of bottles recalled because of bacteria
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled almost 5 million bottles of Fabuloso multipurpose cleaner due to concerns about bacterial contamination, specifically Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall was initiated because a preservative was not added at intended levels during manufacturing, posing a risk of serious infection to individuals with weakened immune systems or underlying health conditions. Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled products immediately and contact Colgate-Palmolive for a refund or replacement.

title: CVS buys primary care provider Oak Street for $10.6 billion
summary: CVS Health is acquiring primary care provider Oak Street Health for approximately $10.6 billion, paying $39 per share in cash. This acquisition deepens CVS's presence in primary care, particularly in value-based care arrangements for Medicare Advantage patients, aligning with federal efforts to cut costs and improve health outcomes. The deal follows other major investments by CVS and rivals like UnitedHealth Group and Walgreens into primary care services.

title: Fabuloso recall: Colgate-Palmolive recalls 4.9M cleaners over bacteria risk
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled 4.9 million bottles of its Fabuloso Multi-Purpose Cleaner due to a risk of bacteria exposure, specifically Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall affects certain scents and bottle sizes sold nationwide since December 2022. Consumers are advised to stop using the product and contact Colgate-Palmolive for a refund or replacement.

title: Colgate-Palmolive recalls 4.9 million bottles of Fabuloso
summary: Colgate-Palmolive has recalled approximately 4.9 million bottles of Fabuloso Multi-Purpose Cleaners due to a risk of exposure to Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall affects products sold between December 2022 and January 2023 at various retailers, posing a serious infection risk for individuals with weakened immune systems. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the recalled products, take a picture of the UPC and lot code, and contact Colgate-Palmolive for a full refund or replacement.

title: 4.9 million Fabuloso cleaning products recalled due to bacteria risk
summary: Colgate-Palmolive Company has recalled approximately 4.9 million units of Fabuloso Multi-Purpose Cleaner products in the U.S. and 56,000 in Canada due to a risk of bacteria contamination, specifically Pseudomonas species bacteria. The recall, impacting products produced between December 14, 2022, and January 23, 2023, is due to inadequate preservative levels during manufacturing. Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled products, which were sold at major retailers, and contact the company for a refund or replacement.

title: Here’s Some Wisdom: Expect the Unexpected
summary: The article discusses tough investing lessons from 2022, a year marked by high inflation, aggressive monetary policy, and geopolitical conflict, which challenged conventional investment wisdom. It covers five key lessons: the failure of traditional diversification, the unpredictable impact of rising rates on stocks, the vulnerability of sustainable investments to market cycles, the risks of thematic investing, and the fact that private markets do not always go up. The author emphasizes the importance of accepting uncertainty in investing, preparing for the unexpected, and focusing on fundamental factors over macro timing.

title: A new era for discoveries at Admera Health
summary: Admera Health, a lab providing genomic and bioinformatic services, is expanding its next-generation sequencing capabilities through strategic investments in advanced technology. With CEO Yun Zhao at the helm, the company works with various clients globally, from biotech firms to universities, focusing on human, animal, and plant health. Admera's adoption of Illumina NovaSeq 6000 and the upcoming NovaSeq X Plus enables faster turnaround times, increased sequencing capacity, and higher quality data, marking a new phase of growth and discovery for the company.

title: Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to the NANC Unusual Whales Subversive Democratic Trading ETF, offering detailed information on its stock profile, price, holdings, expenses, performance, and ESG scores. The ETF, managed by TFG Parent Holdings LLC under the Subversive brand, has an expense ratio of 0.72% and was incepted on February 7, 2023. It outlines key metrics like AUM, top holdings such as NVIDIA, Alphabet, and Microsoft, and various financial charts for analysis.

title: EBay lays off 500 workers
summary: EBay is laying off about 500 employees internationally, representing 4% of its workforce, a move CEO Jamie Iannone states is to invest in new technologies and streamline corporate structure. This follows a trend of layoffs in the retail sector, as companies face financial pressures, with eBay's Q3 revenue declining 5% and gross merchandise volumes dropping 11%. Despite these challenges, eBay continues to invest in new technologies like NFTs and digital collectibles, having acquired KnownOrigin and TCGplayer.

title: Rhode Island Leverages Blockchain Technology for Easier Business
summary: Rhode Island has implemented blockchain technology to streamline the credentialing process for Certified Public Accountants (CPAs), making professional license renewal faster and more efficient. Developed by Infosys Public Services using a distributed ledger on AWS, this solution provides secure digital identities and allows CPAs to store credentials on their phones. The state plans to expand this technology to enable businesses to form LLCs and corporations through a single data entry website, simplifying interactions with government agencies.

title: Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Pro vs. Arlo Pro 3 Floodlight Camera: Which is right for you?
summary: This article compares the Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Pro and the Arlo Pro 3 Floodlight Camera, highlighting their features, pros, and cons to help consumers decide which security camera best fits their needs. Both cameras are priced at $250 and offer robust security features, but differ in video resolution, integration with smart home ecosystems, installation methods, and subscription service benefits. The Ring camera is ideal for Alexa users seeking a hardwired solution with extensive motion detection, while the Arlo excels with 2K HDR video, wireless design, and broader smart assistant compatibility.

title: Diverse Brokers in Bond Issuances
summary: Morgan Stanley is actively working to increase the involvement of minority-owned broker dealers in corporate bond issuances by acting as a diversity and inclusion coordinator. The firm aims to elevate their roles from passive to active co-managers, providing access to broader investor networks and unique insights. This initiative has led to increased partnerships and improved economic payouts for these diversity firms, demonstrating their value beyond just fulfilling DEI objectives.

title: Uber goes multicloud, announcing big deals with Oracle and Google
summary: Uber has announced a multicloud strategy, signing a seven-year partnership with Oracle to move critical workloads to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, a deal estimated to be worth over a billion dollars. Concurrently, Uber is expanding its existing partnership with Google Cloud to modernize its infrastructure and enhance the customer experience. This move aims to accelerate Uber's path to profitability by closing its on-premises data centers and focusing resources on core strengths, while leveraging the price, performance, and flexibility offered by Oracle and Google.

title: Chinese e-commerce giant PDD splashes on Super Bowl ad for its Temu U.S. shopping site
summary: Chinese e-commerce giant PDD Holdings Inc. ran a commercial for its U.S. shopping app, Temu, during the Super Bowl. This costly ad spot signifies Temu's aggressive ambition to penetrate the U.S. e-commerce market, following a strategy of offering heavily discounted products. Temu, which launched in the U.S. in September, has quickly gained popularity, ranking high on app store charts and achieving significant gross merchandise value.

title: Akamai Stock Gains as Earnings Top Estimates. It's Taking On the Cloud Giants.
summary: Akamai Technologies reported better-than-expected earnings, leading to a rise in its stock price. The company is positioning itself to compete with cloud computing giants like Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet by unveiling a new platform for cloud computing, security, and content delivery.

title: The Coca-Cola Company Joins National Museum of African American History and Culture’s Corporate Leadership Council With $1 Million Contribution
summary: The Coca-Cola Company has contributed $1 million to the Smithsonian’s National Museum of African American History and Culture (NMAAHC), joining its Corporate Leadership Council. This expands Coca-Cola's existing support, which includes a $1.25 million founding grant in 2011 from The Coca-Cola Foundation. The company emphasizes its commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, recognizing the Museum's role in preserving African American history and inspiring a barrier-free future.

title: 持续动荡！这一美股巨头首席商务官将离职！又要新一轮裁员？去年宣布裁员1.1万人
summary: Meta Platforms (META)首席商务官Marne Levine宣布将于今年夏天离职，此前她已在公司工作13年。此消息发布之际，Meta正面临营收下滑和可能的新一轮裁员。去年11月，Meta已经裁员1.1万人，占员工总数的13%。

title: Walmart shuts the door on e-commerce-only stores
summary: Walmart is closing its two remaining e-commerce-only stores in Bentonville, Arkansas, and Lincolnwood, Illinois, ending a nearly decade-long experiment focused on improving convenience for online customers. The company explained that these dedicated e-commerce facilities are no longer necessary as it has integrated pickup and delivery services into thousands of its full-service locations. Additionally, Walmart is closing several conventional stores in Illinois, New Mexico, Florida, and Wisconsin by March 10 due to underperformance.

title: KB Securities launches AI-based RoboNews on US stocks
summary: KB Securities has launched KB RoboNews, an AI-based service offering in-depth analysis of public disclosure information for US-listed companies. Developed in collaboration with Whisper, the service analyzes around 3,000 major US stocks, providing insights on investor movements, trading trends, and virtual investment reports. Clients can access this data via KB Securities' M-able Mini mobile trading system.

title: Hedge Fund and Insider Trading News: George Soros, Seth Klarman, D.E. Shaw, Millennium Management, Element Capital, Coliseum Capital Management, Renaissance Technologies, Clearfield Inc (CLFD), Alset Inc. (AEI), and More
summary: This article provides an overview of recent activities in the hedge fund world, including D.E. Shaw closing its first private equity fund, Seth Klarman increasing stakes in Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta, and George Soros' fund investments. It also covers Millennium Management's hiring of a star macro manager, Element Capital's rule relaxation after a significant loss, and a proxy battle involving Coliseum Capital Management and Purple Innovation. The report highlights a strong month for Asia-focused hedge funds, increased scrutiny for crypto's hedge fund ties, Renaissance Technologies' substantial increase in Tesla shares, and insider buying in Clearfield Inc. and Alset Inc.

title: Akamai Stock Tumbles on New Cloud Computing Push
summary: Akamai Technologies (AKAM) stock tumbled after its fourth-quarter earnings report, not primarily due to the results themselves, but because of a major shift in strategy towards aggressive expansion in the highly competitive cloud computing market. The company plans substantial capital spending to build out its new Akamai Connected Cloud, aiming for cloud computing to eventually account for most of its revenue. Analysts expressed concern over the increased risk and competition with hyperscale cloud providers, leading to ratings downgrades and a significant drop in stock price.

title: SaaS company Blackbaud closes four data centers as it moves to the cloud
summary: Blackbaud, a Software-as-a-Service company specializing in CRM and analytics for non-profits, has closed four colocation data centers as part of its migration to cloud platforms like AWS and Azure. The move aims to reduce complexity and costs, despite a recent 10.8 percent revenue growth. The company plans further data center closures and network shutdowns, following a trend seen with other tech giants like Uber.

title: The 7 Best ChatGPT Stocks to Buy Now
summary: This article identifies seven top stocks poised to benefit from the rise of ChatGPT and AI, focusing on companies with established AI development rather than speculative firms. It highlights Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Alphabet (GOOG), Amazon (AMZN), Meta Platforms (META), Microsoft (MSFT), NVIDIA (NVDA), and Salesforce (CRM) as strong investment opportunities. The author emphasizes scrutinizing a company's long-term AI commitment and business model integration to avoid hype-driven investments.

title: Dissecting the Chamber’s stance on climate policies
summary: A report by InfluenceMap indicates that the U.S. Chamber of Commerce’s climate policy positions largely align with its fossil fuel members, earning it a low E- score for 25 out of 39 negative policy stances last year. Despite claims of advocating for climate solutions, the Chamber opposed key legislation like the Inflation Reduction Act, frequently adopting high-level positive statements that contradict its specific opposition to regulations. The Chamber, however, asserts that its opposition to the IRA was tax-related and that it actively supports other climate-advancing initiatives.

title: WPP partners with Stripe to expand commerce and payments solutions for brands
summary: WPP has partnered with Stripe to expand its commerce and payments solutions, becoming a Consulting Partner within the Stripe Partner Ecosystem. This collaboration aims to help clients with digital transformation, e-commerce, and mobile applications, leveraging WPP's 13,500 commerce specialists and Stripe's financial infrastructure. The partnership addresses the growing trend of online spending and the increasing demand for integrated brand and commerce strategies to enhance customer experience.

title: Amazon asks employees to be in office at least three days a week
summary: Amazon announced that effective May 1, employees would be required to work from the office at least three days a week, a shift from previous, more flexible remote work policies implemented during the pandemic. CEO Andy Jassy stated this decision would enhance learning and collaboration and boost businesses near Amazon's urban headquarters. Some exceptions will be made for specific roles like customer support and sales.

title: Funding Roundup: Crypto Companies Landed $185M This Week
summary: Crypto and Web3 companies raised a cumulative $185 million this week, a decrease from the previous week's total of $213 million. The majority of this funding went to pre-seed or seed rounds for startups focusing on building Web3 infrastructure. Notable funding rounds included Taurus securing $65 million, Superplastic raising $20 million, and Monad Labs receiving $19 million.

title: Kroger workers who quit are getting texts and emails from the company asking them to come back
summary: Kroger, the largest supermarket operator in the U.S. by sales, is actively reaching out to former employees via texts and emails, encouraging them to return. This unusual recruitment strategy is a response to the current low unemployment rate and the competitive job market, with Kroger's chief people officer stating that "alumni are also a talent source." The company has found that returning workers are often more productive than new hires and has seen success in re-recruiting individuals, sometimes offering higher salaries.

title: Veritone Q4 Earnings Preview: Going Nowhere (NASDAQ:VERI)
summary: Veritone's shares have seen a significant rebound this year, largely due to a new cost-cutting plan. However, the company faces stagnation in its core business, exhibiting only single-digit growth when acquisitions are excluded. Furthermore, Veritone lags behind better-branded AI competitors like C3.ai and carries a substantial revenue risk due to its over 30% concentration with Amazon, which is actively seeking to reduce costs.

title: FTC Alleges Supplement Company ‘Hijacked’ Amazon Reviews to Boost Sales
summary: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has taken its first enforcement action against "review hijacking," fining Bountiful Co. $600,000. The nutritional supplement company is accused of manipulating Amazon reviews to make some of its products appear to have more reviews and higher ratings than they actually did. Bountiful Co. stated it used Amazon’s “variation” feature to highlight similar products and denied deceiving shoppers.

title: Why Missouri has seen a wave of distribution center openings
summary: Missouri has become a popular location for distribution and fulfillment centers due to its central geographic location, offering reduced transportation costs and faster delivery times across the U.S. Companies like Urban Outfitters and Chewy have capitalized on the state's strategic position and strong labor market. While warehouse rents have risen, the benefits of lower transportation costs and quicker transit times often outweigh increased lease agreements, although sustaining this growth might face challenges due to a tightening local real estate market.

title: Lessons from transformers: How some distributors reset and won
summary: This article examines how a small group of distributors are outperforming their peers in a challenging marketplace by transforming their business models. They achieve this through strategic M&A, a relentless focus on customer satisfaction, expanding product assortments and value-added services, and leveraging digital experiences. The piece outlines five key practices for success, including building M&A capabilities, pursuing holistic and profitable growth, understanding customer needs, and making strategic digital investments.

title: NVIDIA GTC 2023 to Feature Latest Advances in AI Computing Systems, Generative AI, Industrial Metaverse, Robotics; Keynote by Jensen Huang; Talks by OpenAI, DeepMind Founders
summary: NVIDIA announced its GTC 2023 conference, scheduled for March 20-23, will feature a keynote by CEO Jensen Huang focusing on generative AI, the metaverse, large language models, and robotics. The virtual event expects over 250,000 registrants and more than 650 sessions, including talks from leaders like OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever and DeepMind's Demis Hassabis. GTC 2023 will also offer learning opportunities, dedicated sessions for startups, and a financial analyst Q&A session.

title: Focus: ChatGPT launches boom in AI-written e-books on Amazon
summary: The launch of ChatGPT has led to a proliferation of AI-written e-books on Amazon, with hundreds already listed and the number growing daily. Authors are using the AI software to quickly generate content for books, ranging from children's stories to novellas and self-help guides, often without disclosing AI's involvement. This trend raises concerns among human authors and organizations like the Authors Guild about potential market saturation with low-quality content and the commoditization of writing.

title: One Medical joins Amazon to make it easier for people to get and stay healthier
summary: Amazon has completed its acquisition of One Medical, aiming to enhance access to quality, convenient, and affordable primary care. Following the acquisition, Amazon and One Medical plan to expand their human-centered and technology-powered healthcare model, offering services from virtual care to in-office visits and specialized programs. For a limited time, One Medical is offering new members a discounted annual membership at $144 for the first year.

title: A Supplement Company 'Hijacked' Its Amazon Reviews to Boost Sales, According to the FTC
summary: The Federal Trade Commission fined The Bountiful Company $600,000 for "review hijacking" on Amazon. The supplement maker allegedly exploited Amazon's variation policy to group new or poorly performing products with established, highly-rated ones, artificially boosting their reviews and sales. This practice, described by the FTC as false advertising, involved linking products with different ingredients and formulations, misleading consumers and potentially posing safety risks.

title: Target Investing $100 Million in Sortation, Speeding Up Online Orders
summary: Target is investing $100 million into its supply chain sortation network to accelerate online order fulfillment. The company plans to add more than six new sortation centers by the end of 2026, bringing the total to over 15, which will enhance its next-day delivery capabilities and feed packages to its Shipt service. This expansion aims to increase speed and precision, control costs, and leverage Target's stores-as-hubs strategy for faster, more cost-effective delivery.

title: Amazon completes One Medical takeover after FTC nod, discounts membership
summary: Amazon announced the completion of its $3.5 billion acquisition of primary care provider One Medical, following the FTC's decision not to challenge the deal. This move marks Amazon's entry into in-person medical services and expands its virtual health offerings, despite previous challenges in the healthcare sector. Amazon is also offering a discounted first-year membership for One Medical to attract new customers.

title: Can PDD’s share price maintain its streak following Temu’s debut?
summary: PDD Holdings' ecommerce app, Temu, made its Super Bowl debut as part of an aggressive push into the North American market, following China's Shein with a discount pricing strategy. Temu has seen rapid growth in downloads and gross merchandise value since its US launch, despite facing stiff competition from established players like Amazon, Shein, and AliExpress. The article also examines the performance of relevant ETFs, including the Global X Emerging Markets Internet & E-commerce ETF and the Invesco Golden Dragon China ETF, both of which hold PDD.

title: HPE boss Antonio Neri paid as much as 271 employees in 2022
summary: HPE CEO Antonio Neri received $17.36 million in compensation for fiscal year 2022, which is equivalent to the average annual pay of 271 HPE employees. The company's revenue grew by 3 percent to $28.5 billion, while Neri's total compensation was slightly down from the previous year. The article also notes the challenges HPE faces from cloud giants and its "Greenlake" as-a-service offerings.

title: Roku, Best Buy Partner for SXSW Confab Exhibit March 11-12
summary: Roku is partnering with Best Buy to host its first-ever South by Southwest (SXSW) conference pop-up display called “Roku City featuring the Best Buy Home Theater Experience.” The activation, open to the public March 11-12 in Austin, aims to bring the "Roku City" screensaver to life as an interactive experience, including a style shop, a rooftop diner, and a Best Buy Home Theater Experience. This collaboration seeks to spark conversations about brand activation based on audience feedback and the value of in-person experiences in a digital world.

title: Netflix plunges after the streaming giant launches a wave of price cuts in 100 countries in the face of stiff competition
summary: Netflix's stock dropped 5% on Thursday following reports that the company is implementing significant price cuts across over 100 countries, affecting more than 10 million subscribers. These price reductions, some as high as 50%, mark a shift from Netflix's previous strategy of raising prices and come amid increased competition in the streaming market and efforts to curb password sharing. The company aims to improve member experience and offer more affordable options, as evidenced by its recent ad-supported subscription tier.

title: Amazon Launches OEM Auto Parts Store
summary: Amazon has launched a new OEM Parts Shop, building on its existing Amazon Garage, to offer aftermarket replacement and custom parts from various automotive brands including GM, Stellantis, BMW, and Yamaha. This move is seen as a response to the growth of eBay Motors and aims to simplify the automotive parts shopping experience for customers. The new shop provides detailed product information, transparent pricing, and multiple delivery options, allowing customers to easily find parts using vehicle specifications.

title: 18 Ways to Make Money Online and Offline in Canada
summary: This article from NerdWallet Canada outlines 18 legitimate ways for Canadians to earn money, both online and offline. It covers opportunities ranging from selling collectibles and offering freelance services to house-sitting and dog walking, providing details on setup, costs, and earning potential for each method. The guide also includes specific sections for teens and advice on making money in other countries.

title: Court rejects deception charges against Savers Value Village
summary: The Washington state Supreme Court has unanimously ruled in favor of Savers Value Village, rejecting deception charges brought by Attorney General Bob Ferguson. The court found that the thrift store chain's marketing practices, which emphasize its work with charities, constitute protected free speech. Despite the ruling, Ferguson's office expressed disappointment and noted that their investigation led Value Village to change its marketing practices to more clearly disclose its for-profit status.

title: Amazon Takes Over One Medical Primary Care Service, Which Includes San Diego Market
summary: Amazon has completed its $3.5 billion acquisition of primary care provider One Medical, after the FTC decided not to challenge the deal. This move allows Amazon to enter the virtual and in-person healthcare services market, aiming to simplify healthcare navigation. One Medical, which had 836,000 members and $1 billion in net revenue in 2022, will now offer discounted memberships to new customers.

title: Amazon's Lagging Performance Vs. eBay Since 2020 Should Continue
summary: The author reiterates a successful spread trade strategy involving going long on eBay (EBAY) and short on Amazon (AMZN), which has performed well since late 2020 and is suggested to continue in 2023. This recommendation is based on the belief that eBay is undervalued despite slow growth, while Amazon remains overvalued, particularly if a recession occurs, due to its slim margins. The article emphasizes that eBay's future value is often misunderstood, while Amazon's valuation is seen as unsustainable under potential economic pressures.

title: GSMA debuts open API toolkit as AWS and Microsoft roll out new carrier offerings
summary: The GSMA Association introduced its Open Gateway toolkit at MWC Barcelona 2023, designed to allow carriers to make their networks accessible through interoperable APIs, fostering development across multiple carrier networks. Simultaneously, Amazon Web Services Inc. and Microsoft Corp. unveiled new offerings aimed at simplifying cloud adoption for carriers, including collaborations with Nokia Corp. and Juniper Networks Inc. The Open Gateway, backed by 21 carriers, is based on the open-source CAMARA toolkit and seeks to integrate mobile operators and cloud services.

title: SaksOff5th.com beefs up user experience leadership
summary: SaksOff5th.com has appointed Julie Mares as Senior Vice President of E-commerce to enhance its user experience and omnichannel strategy. Mares, previously from Untuckit and with over two decades of retail experience, will report to SaksOff5th.com CEO Paige Thomas and focus on the end-to-end customer journey. This move follows recent layoffs at the company, indicating a strategic shift towards prioritizing digital capabilities and customer-facing initiatives after focusing on supply chain issues.

title: How Have the Top U.S. Asset Managers Voted in 2022?
summary: This article analyzes how the top U.S. asset managers voted on key environmental and social shareholder resolutions in 2022, comparing trends across 2020-2022. It highlights a significant increase in social and environmental resolutions and varying support levels among major asset managers, especially the "Big Three" (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street). The report also examines how sustainable funds within these managers voted compared to their wider fund ranges.

title: Focus: Aviation industry turns to childcare, free iPhones to lure workers
summary: The North American aviation industry is implementing new strategies like offering childcare, cheaper transportation, and free iPhones to attract and retain workers. This comes as the industry struggles with worker shortages and high turnover rates, where salaries for entry-level jobs often lag behind e-commerce companies. These initiatives aim to address the challenges of unsocial working hours and reduce the worker shortage that led to significant disruptions last year.

title: Start of a New Era: Why Nokia has changed its logo for the first time in 60 years
summary: Nokia has changed its logo for the first time in 60 years, redesigning it to shed its association with mobile phones and signal a shift towards being a "business technology company." CEO Pekka Lundmark aims to expand Nokia's focus on selling networking gear to other businesses, moving beyond its traditional telecom service provider segment. This strategic redirection includes increasing market share in enterprise business and reviewing growth paths for different units, spurred partly by restrictions on rival Huawei Technologies.

title: PWB Top Holdings List & Exposure (Invesco Large Cap Growth ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the Invesco Large Cap Growth ETF (PWB) as of May 22, 2026. Key holdings include Advanced Micro Devices, Micron Technology, and Amazon.com, with the top 25 making up over 70% of the fund. The ETF primarily invests in North American large-cap companies, with significant exposure to the Technology sector and the United States geographically.

title: Amazon closes, cancels more warehouses as cost-cutting persists
summary: Amazon continues to reduce its fulfillment network as part of a cost-cutting initiative, canceling, closing, or delaying 99 facilities, impacting nearly 32.3 million square feet of space. While Amazon disputes the exact figures from consulting firm MWPVL International, CEO Andy Jassy has emphasized that reducing operational costs is a top priority for 2023. Despite these closures, Amazon still plans to open 231 new facilities, though some of these openings may be at risk due to ongoing cost-cutting efforts.

title: Better Launches Newest Mortgage Innovation ‘Equity Unlocker’ to Help Tech Employees Purchase Homes
summary: Better Mortgage has introduced "Equity Unlocker," a new program for tech employees, starting with Amazon, that allows them to use vested equity as collateral for a home down payment instead of selling shares. This innovation aims to address the challenges millennials face in homeownership due to student loans and an affordability crisis. The program is currently available in Florida, New York, and Washington, with plans for nationwide expansion and inclusion of other companies' employees.

title: ITAN Top Holdings List & Exposure (Sparkline Intangible Value ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the Sparkline Intangible Value ETF (ITAN). It lists the ETF's top 25 stock holdings by weight, including major companies like Amazon.com, Intel, and Cisco Systems, which collectively represent 41.86% of the fund. The article also breaks down ITAN's geographic, currency, sector, industry, and sub-industry exposures, showing a dominant allocation to the United States and the Technology sector.

title: Thoughtworks tops fourth-quarter estimates, but stock tumbles 17%+
summary: Despite exceeding fourth-quarter revenue and EPS estimates, Thoughtworks Holding Inc.'s stock fell over 17% due to a pessimistic first-quarter outlook, which projects a low single-digit revenue decline. The technology consultancy reported an 8.3% year-over-year revenue increase to $310.7 million in Q4 and a net income of $16.1 million, but forecasts a 5% to 5.5% revenue decrease for the current quarter before an anticipated return to growth for the full fiscal year 2023.

title: Cloud kitchen operator Rebel Foods to run 150 Wendy’s restaurants in India
summary: Wendy's Co. has partnered with cloud kitchen operator Rebel Foods Pvt to significantly expand its physical presence in India, aiming for 150 traditional restaurant locations over the next decade. This new deal builds on their previous agreement for 250 cloud kitchens in India. Rebel Foods will leverage its digital expertise in delivery and automation to help grow the Wendy's brand, which already customizes its menu for the Indian palate.

title: IOO Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares Global 100 ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed look at the iShares Global 100 ETF (IOO) holdings. It lists the top 25 stocks by weight, including NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft, which collectively account for over 75% of the fund. The article also breaks down IOO's exposure by geographic region, currency, sector, and industry for investors.

title: CRBN Top Holdings List & Exposure (iShares MSCI ACWI Low Carbon Target ETF)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure of the iShares MSCI ACWI Low Carbon Target ETF (CRBN). It provides a ranked list of the top 25 companies by weight, which collectively comprise 35.50% of the fund. The article also breaks down CRBN's exposure across geographic regions, currencies, sectors, industries, and sub-industries, highlighting significant allocations to the United States, USD, and the Technology sector.

title: XLY Top Holdings List & Exposure (Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund)
summary: This article details the top holdings and exposure breakdown for the Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLY). It lists the top 25 stock holdings by weight, including Amazon.com and Tesla, which together comprise a significant portion of the fund. The report also outlines XLY's major geographic, currency, sector, industry, and sub-industry exposures.

title: XLG Top Holdings List & Exposure (Invesco S&P 500 Top 50 ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed look at the Invesco S&P 500 Top 50 ETF (XLG), including its top 25 holdings by weight, geographic exposure, currency exposure, and sector and industry breakdowns. NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft are identified as the leading holdings. The fund primarily invests in large-cap US companies with significant exposure to the technology sector.

title: PY Top Holdings List & Exposure (Principal Value ETF)
summary: This article provides a detailed look at the Principal Value ETF (PY), including its top 25 stock holdings by weight, with Apple, Walmart, and Amazon leading the list. It also breaks down the ETF's exposure across various geographic regions, currencies, sectors, industries, and sub-industries. The fund primarily invests in North American equities, with a significant concentration in the United States and within the Financials and Technology sectors.
